diagram.caption: THE DEMAND ENGINE

sections.heading: What B2B Demand Generation Actually Means
intro: Demand generation is the coordinated work of creating awareness and preference, capturing existing intent and helping the right buyers move towards a commercial conversation.

It is broader than lead generation and more accountable than simply calling something brand. The job is to build a repeatable connection between market, message, programmes, buyer behaviour and pipeline.

sections.heading: A B2B Demand Generation Strategy Starts Before the Channels
sections.intro: Commview does not arrive with a channel quota. We work out what the business needs to change, then choose the programmes that fit the buying motion.

items.title: Customer and ICP
items.body: Know which accounts and people the programme is actually trying to influence.

items.title: Position and message
items.body: Give the market a reason to notice, understand and prefer the offer.

items.title: Create demand
items.body: Use useful content, events, paid activity, community or ABM where they fit the audience.

items.title: Capture demand
items.body: Make it easy for existing intent to find the right page, proof, conversation or next step.

items.title: Connect Sales
items.body: Route useful signals and commercial context rather than throwing disconnected leads over a wall.

items.title: Measure and learn
items.body: Use downstream evidence to change targeting, message, programme mix and investment.

sections.heading: Build a Demand Generation Programme That Learns
sections.intro: Campaigns end. A demand engine should become better at deciding where to spend attention and money.

steps.title: Diagnose
steps.body: Find the commercial constraint before choosing the tactic.

steps.title: Design
steps.body: Connect audience, message, channel, offer and sales motion.

steps.title: Run
steps.body: Execute the work rather than handing the plan to somebody else by default.

steps.title: Measure
steps.body: Look beyond surface engagement to the commercial behaviour that follows.

steps.title: Learn
steps.body: Feed sales and customer evidence back into the next programme decision.

items.q: How is demand generation different from lead generation?
items.a: Demand generation creates and captures interest across the buying journey, including activity that may not produce an immediate lead. Lead generation focuses more narrowly on identifying or collecting prospects for follow-up. A good B2B system connects both, but it does not treat every piece of attention as a lead.

items.q: What does a demand generation consultant do?
items.a: A demand generation consultant helps decide who to target, what the market needs to hear, which programmes can create or capture demand, how activity connects to Sales and how performance should be measured. At Commview, that can include hands-on execution as well as strategy rather than stopping at a campaign plan.

items.q: Do you run the demand generation programmes as well as plan them?
items.a: Yes, where that is the right engagement. Commview can write emails, shape content, review SEO and paid activity, analyse conversion and coordinate specialist execution. The aim is to keep strategy close enough to delivery that we can see whether the commercial hypothesis is actually working and change it when needed.

sections.heading: Stop asking which channel you need. Start with what is stopping demand from becoming pipeline.
sections.body: We can diagnose the constraint, design the programme and stay close enough to execution to see whether it works.
